scientific_target.question: How accurately can predictions using permitted M1/S1 calcium and context improve held-out joint angles over an independently fixed target/phase/coarse-motion model, and how does prediction gain vary between areas within the same five mice?
scientific_target.known_answer: Actual held-out 24-joint trajectories establish prediction losses; the signed incremental EV and paired S1-minus-M1 contrasts are recomputed from those measurements and submitted predictions, never supplied by a favored paper conclusion.
scientific_target.answer_origin: Native jointAngles synchronized to the same original calcium trial; the current trusted procedure outputs are calibration references, not ground-truth joint angles.
scientific_target.case_unit: Complete session fold: 5 mice × 2 areas × 5 whole-trial folds = 50 computational cases, with all 51 time points and 24 angles.
scientific_target.independent_unit: Five paired mice; session days differ between M1 and S1, so matched counts do not create paired individual reaches.
scientific_target.inference_scope: Within-mouse retrospective measured-kinematics prediction. Gain over the fixed regularized nuisance learner does not identify neural dependence: an arbitrary candidate can improve context modeling. Neural attribution additionally requires matched candidate context-only and neural-disruption ablations; no nuisance-free information or causal necessity claim follows.
exclusions: No reward for copying the author or benchmark algorithm.
No claim of native interpretation from fixed-procedure reconstruction.
No 50-independent-animal, cross-animal transfer or exact historical Figure 5 reproduction claim.
Positive fixed-nuisance prediction gain alone establishes calcium information rather than improved context modeling.

inputs: Per-fold x: trial×51×128 ROI calcium features; z: trial×51×141 fixed nuisance features; training y: trial×51×24 original angles.

Nuisance basis has target×time indicators, target-interacted phase/duration terms, centroid position/velocity and quadratic terms; target, lift/grab timing and coarse motion are explicitly retrospective inputs.
forbidden_inputs: Query joint angles, individual target-marker coordinates, query target-validity masks and target-derived extra features.
Other folds or aligned full-session arrays during a case: each fold training set contains labels for another fold query set.
Candidate-controlled nuisance predictions as the primary gain anchor; revised scoring fixes these in the operator.
observation_contract.case_identity: Current design enumerates all 50 mouse/area/fold cases and whole original trial IDs. Matching uses first chronological min(N_M1,N_S1) trials per reach target, requiring at least ten per target/area and 128 eligible ROIs; authentic counts are not yet prepared.
observation_contract.split: Current source uses target-stratified trial ordinal modulo five and complete training complements; each original session trial is query exactly once. Freeze the native source predicate and alignment before outcome access.
observation_contract.coverage: Complete five-mouse/ten-session/50-fold domain and all 240 mouse-area-joint effects required; the current source estimates do not establish real packet coverage or authentic ten-recording preparation.

primary.name: equal_mouse_area_joint_fixed_nuisance_incremental_EV
primary.aggregation: Implemented additive scorer pools each session joint query SSE/SST across all five folds once; ΔEV=(SSE_operator_fixed_nuisance−SSE_candidate_prediction)/SST, equal24 joints, two areas per mouse and five mice, retaining all signed values.
primary.rationale: Recorded angles are the target and independently frozen nuisance predictions are the comparison anchor. Candidate nuisance degradation cannot raise the primary. Arbitrary permitted methods are allowed; closeness to the fixed analysis is only a separate legacy calibration endpoint.

secondary: All240 per-joint gains, candidate and fixed nuisance/neural/shifted MSEs, candidate/nuisance R² and signed fixed-reference comparisons.
Five mouse-level gains and descriptive S1−M1 differences; the new scorer supplies no inferential interval or p-value.

Matched candidate context-only and neural-disruption ablations under equal fitting/selection budgets are required separately before attributing gain to neural observations. The fixed shifted reference is not a matched arbitrary-candidate ablation.
Unchanged legacy reconstruction MAE and historical sign-flip/t95/Holm diagnostics remain calibration-only outputs, never silently combined with the new primary.

evaluation.uncertainty: Five mice, not50 folds or240 joint effects, are biological units. New measured-target scorer reports complete descriptive mouse/area values without intervals or significance. Legacy32 sign-flip/t95/Holm outputs retain their own historical assumptions and are not new-score inference.
evaluation.failure_policy: Require exact50-case identity, complete ordered query trials and every51×24 trajectory. New candidate schema needs trial_id and neural predictions only; legacy3-arm artifacts are compatible, but their nuisance/shifted values cannot affect the primary. Undefined joint variance or arithmetic overflow/underflow refuses the complete score. CLI requires independently supplied operator design/binding hashes and pinned target/reference arrays.
